record.paper_title: Brownian models of multiclass queueing networks: Current status and open problems
record.context_brief: Existence and uniqueness of the reduced Brownian system model
record.original_question: Let d be the number of stations, let G be the d x d routing-information matrix, let theta be the vector of netflow rates, and let Gamma be the covariance matrix in the Brownian approximation. If xi-star is a d-dimensional Brownian motion with drift minus theta and covariance Gamma, does there exist a unique nonnegative process W-star together with a continuous, nondecreasing regulator Y-star such that W-star(t) = xi-star(t) - G W-star(t) + Y-star(t) for all t, with each coordinate Y-star_j allowed to increase only when the corresponding coordinate W-star_j is zero?

evidence.quote: The question remains as to whether for general (θ, Γ, G) there exists a process W* that satisfies (4.24)-(4.28) and whether this process is unique. Although there are partial answers to this question, no definitive account has been given for this problem. This issue must be resolved in order for the Brownian approximation to be fully "justified",

artifact.category_tag: Reflecting Brownian motion in an orthant
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent to the original posing of this question, Reiman and Williams (1988) proved that the "completely-S" condition on the reflection matrix R = I+G is necessary for existence of a semimartingale reflecting Brownian motion (SRBM) in the nonnegative orthant, and Taylor and Williams (1993) proved it is sufficient and yields uniqueness in law. Hence for the orthant case the existence/uniqueness question is essentially resolved. Generalizations to nonsimple convex polyhedra and stronger pathwise-uniqueness statements remain partially open.

status_evidence.title: Existence and uniqueness of semimartingale reflecting Brownian motions in an orthant (Taylor & Williams)
status_evidence.snippet: Existence and uniqueness of SRBMs in an orthant under the completely-S condition on the reflection matrix.
status_evidence.claim: The existence/uniqueness problem for SRBM in the nonnegative orthant was resolved by Taylor–Williams (1993) under the completely-S condition, with necessity established earlier by Reiman–Williams.

status_evidence.title: Existence and Uniqueness of Semimartingale Reflecting Brownian Motions in Convex Polyhedrons
status_evidence.snippet: Necessary and sufficient conditions for existence and uniqueness of SRBM in simple convex polyhedrons; sufficiency in the nonsimple case, with necessity open.
status_evidence.claim: Generalizations beyond the orthant are partially solved; necessity in the nonsimple polyhedral case remains open.
